Triage & ContinuityThe bridge to human care,
not the replacement for it.

The mental-health system loses people twice: once in the months of waiting, and once in the retelling — every new professional, the same story from zero. Triage & Continuity is a check-in and routing system that keeps you moving toward human care, and carries your journey with you.

WHY IT HAS TO EXIST

The waiting room is months long.
And nobody holds your file.

Between the moment someone seeks help and the moment they sit across from a professional lies a gap the system was never built to manage — and a generation of AI chatbots rushed into it with promises they could not keep.

F·01

The wait is the wound

In Germany, analyses prepared for the Bundestag document typical waits of three to six months for a therapy place. Demand for support keeps climbing across Europe — the front door of the system is where people are lost.

F·02

The story resets every time

GP to counsellor to therapist to crisis line — each handover starts from zero, and the retelling itself is a documented burden. Continuity of the journey is the unowned problem in mental-health care.

F·03

The chatbot era overpromised

AI “therapist” apps have ended in shutdowns, FTC action over data sharing, and litigation over harms to vulnerable users. The lesson is not that software has no role — it is that pretending software is a clinician is the wrong role.

F·04

The cost lands everywhere

Deloitte estimates poor mental health costs UK employers around £51 billion a year. Behind the number is the same mechanism: people struggling in the gap before care, invisibly.

GERMANY: 3–6 MONTH TYPICAL WAITS FOR A THERAPY PLACE
WHO IT SERVES

For the person
in the gap.

The person waiting for care

The system’s first user is the person who has already asked for help and been handed a waiting time. Structured check-ins hold the thread, the record grows instead of resetting, and if things worsen, routing escalates — to humans, every time.

ALREADY SEEKING HELPMONTHS FROM A PLACEJOURNEY HELDHUMAN ESCALATION

Families & supporters

The people carrying someone through the wait get guidance on what to watch for and where the real doors are — without ever seeing more than the person chooses to share.

Employers of care

Organisations that want to offer staff something honest: a private check-in and routing tool, structurally incapable of reporting anyone’s inner life to their employer.

Practitioners, on consent

When the user chooses, a professional receives an arrival summary instead of a cold start — the journey so far, in minutes, not the first three sessions.

Underserved regions

Places where the nearest practitioner is a ferry or a hundred kilometres away. Routing knows the real map of available care, including remote options.

WHAT IT CHANGES

Held, routed,
and never asked to start over.

Triage & Continuity does three honest things: it checks in, it routes to human care, and it remembers — with the user owning every word of the record. It does not diagnose, does not treat, and does not pretend.

A thread that holds.

Structured check-ins across the waiting months — a felt trajectory made visible, so neither the person nor their eventual practitioner starts blind.

The right door, faster.

Routing built on the actual care landscape — GPs, therapists, community services, crisis lines — matched to need, location and urgency, with escalation paths that go straight to humans.

Your story, portable.

The journey record belongs to the user, on their device — shared with a chosen professional in one consented handover, never sold, never mined.

THE MECHANICS

On the device.
Off the market.

Data about a person’s inner life is the most sensitive class there is. The architecture answers accordingly: processing on the user’s own device, a record only the user holds, and routing logic that treats escalation to humans as the primary function — not a liability footnote.

LAYER 1

The check-in layer

Brief structured conversations and validated-questionnaire-style self-reports, processed on-device. Designed for consistency over the long haul, not engagement metrics.

LAYER 2

The continuity record

A longitudinal journal of check-ins, encrypted on the user’s device. The user reads it, exports it, deletes it. There is no server-side behavioural profile — by architecture.

LAYER 3

The routing engine

A maintained directory of real care pathways per region, with urgency-aware matching and hard-coded crisis escalation to human services. This layer is the product’s conscience.

LAYER 4

The handover surface

Consented, structured summaries for the professional the user reaches — the journey so far, in clinical-friendly form, generated only when the user says so.
